stages.sub: Why breaking production into separate tasks makes workers more productive.

steps.q: One worker makes a whole pin, or ten workers each do one step. Which way makes more pins a day?
steps.right: Splitting the process into separate steps
steps.wrong: Each worker making a whole pin alone
steps.hint: Think about a worker who only ever does one simple step, over and over.

steps.q: Tasks are now split up. What does each worker end up doing all day?
steps.wrong: Performing several different steps in turn
steps.hint: Splitting the process means each person keeps to one job, not many.

steps.q: A worker doing every step walks between benches and swaps tools. Does a worker who stays at one bench lose that time?
steps.wrong: Yes, they lose the same amount of time
steps.hint: One worker moves between many tasks and tools, the other stays put.

steps.q: A costly machine does just one step of making a pin. Is it worth buying if that step is done all day?
steps.right: Yes, because that one step is done constantly
steps.wrong: No, it would sit idle most of the time
steps.hint: Think about who could keep a specialised machine busy: someone doing many jobs, or someone doing one job all day.
